glance_takeaway: This is a final readout of an onboarding-redesign A/B test ('Pathways', ONB-2026-014) with 184,204 signups over six weeks. The redesign did not win overall — the blended +0.8pp effect on trial-to-paid conversion is inconclusive (CI straddles zero) — because a big mobile-web win (+4.2pp, significant) and an iOS loss (−1.9pp, significant) cancel out, with Android flat. The recommendation is to ship it narrowly on mobile-web and fix iOS; there is also a hint that early weeks overstated the new version due to novelty decay.

F1.note: Forest plot label '+0.8pp' + figcaption defines trial-to-paid ('first payment succeeds within 14 days'); absolute rates 11.4%/12.2% are omitted but the delta and metric are correct.

F2.note: '+0.8pp · CI [−0.3, +1.9] · p = 0.16' with open marker legend 'straddles 0 — inconclusive' and annotation 'the honest overall verdict is can't tell'.

F3.note: Meta line '184,204 randomized · 13,249 trial starters'; forest plot 'n 6,602 / 6,647'; per-arm randomized counts not shown but SRM-clean note covers the 50/50 integrity.

F4.note: Figcaption: 'from an experiment powered only for ±1.55pp overall'.

F5.note: Meta 'platform subgroups pre-registered'; decision figcaption 'the single pre-registered subgroup'.

F6.note: '+4.2pp · CI [+2.1, +6.3] · p < 0.0001' in accent with filled marker; base rates 13.9%/18.1% omitted; Bonferroni survival implicit via p < 0.0001.

F7.note: '−1.9pp · CI [−3.6, −0.2] · p = 0.027'; decision figcaption states it does not survive Bonferroni (α = 0.0167) yet is credible via pre-registration + mechanism.

F9.note: Standfirst 'the blended number hides both' + figcaption 'a strong win and a real loss averaging each other out, not a modest win everywhere'.

F10.note: Line chart labels +2.9, +1.5, +0.6, 0.0, −0.4, +0.1 for wk 1–6; heading 'Early weeks overstated B — novelty decay'.

F11.note: Annotation 'weeks 4–6 (exploratory pooled): mobile-web still +3.8pp, iOS still −2.2pp — the split outlives the novelty'; repeated in the decision table's Weeks 4–6 column.

F12.note: Decision figcaption: retention flat '+0.2pp, CI [−0.2, +0.6]' and '+12% support-ticket blip in weeks 1–2 resolved'; absolute 31.2%/31.4% omitted.

F13.note: Notes: 'time-to-first-lesson fell 38 s (CI [−45, −31])' and 'trial-start rate flat (7.17% vs 7.22%), so the trial-starter denominator is sound'; absolute 292s/254s omitted.

F14.note: Bar chart: iOS 8.1% → 12.7%, mobile-web 3.2% → 3.4%, Android 5.0% → 5.6%, with the OS-dialog mechanism annotation.

F15.note: Decision table: Ship mobile-web with 5% holdback; Do not ship iOS (fix experiment ONB-2026-019, prompt reverted to day-2 soft ask) or Android; notes say 'no sample-ratio mismatch' (SRM p-value itself omitted).

render_issues: Forest-plot annotation clipped at the right SVG viewBox edge: 'overall verdict is "can't tell," not "B won"' renders as '... not "i' in both glance.png and full.png (text x=568 overruns the 832-unit viewBox). The weeks 4-6 annotation also runs close to the figure edge. Everything else renders cleanly.
strengths: The forest plot's open-vs-filled marker encoding makes 'CI straddles zero' visually distinct from significant effects — exactly the uncertainty-at-a-glance requirement in the brief — and headline + standfirst land the split, the non-win, and the narrow decision within seconds.

Exceptional fact retention: all 15 key facts survive with correct numbers, direction, and significance status, including the hard-to-keep caveats (±1.55pp powering, Bonferroni hedge, exploratory funnel-data confound, 'don't cite the week-2 interim').
weaknesses: The most rhetorically important annotation on the page — the 'can't tell, not B won' callout on the forest plot — is truncated by the SVG viewBox, so its punchline is literally cut off.
Absolute conversion levels are never shown (11.4% vs 12.2%, mobile-web 13.9% -> 18.1%, retention 31.2%/31.4%), so a PM cannot gauge relative magnitude or recompute anything from base rates.
evaluator_notes: Editorial single-column layout with three hand-built SVG figures (forest plot, decay line, grouped bars) and a decision table. Encodings are honest: consistent 40px-per-pp scale in the forest plot, zero lines marked, significance encoded by marker fill rather than color alone. Density is high but well matched to a stats-literate PM; jargon (Bonferroni, SRM) is glossed inline. Accuracy scored 10.0 by formula (15 conveyed, 0 distorted/contradicted); several facts omit absolute base rates, which is noted per-fact but does not constitute distortion. Visual craft held down by the clipped annotation, an avoidable layout bug in an otherwise disciplined page. Overall = 0.35*10.0 + 0.30*9.0 + 0.15*8.5 + 0.10*8.5 + 0.10*7.5 = 9.075 -> 9.1.
